source: Curated from web literature search and Europe PMC harvest (fixtures/europepmc_npy_pdx1_harvest.json)
curationNote: Matches are limited to what each abstract or page states. Items marked abstract-head were read only as far as the stored abstract head; none of these papers tested an NPY to PDX1 wire directly.

literature.finding: NPY marks partially differentiated beta cells. It is excluded from Pdx1-positive progenitors at E12.5, falls after birth (about 48% of islet cells at P0 to 3.5% at P30), and is re-expressed under high-fat diet (about 2% to 15%), in db/db and in NOD mice. NPY knockdown reduces replication and enhances glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
literature.bearsOn: Direction of the wire: NPY is high where Pdx1 maturity is low and returns under stress.

literature.finding: Pdx1 deletion in ducts leaves postnatal beta-cell formation intact but impairs maturation. PDX1-low beta cells coexpress MAFB and NPY/PYY (the antibody cannot separate the two). PYY mRNA is elevated; NPY and PP mRNA are not.
literature.bearsOn: Same direction from the Pdx1 side, with a qualifier: the NPY signal in that study is not cleanly separated from PYY.

literature.finding: Pdx1 and Oc1 cooperate in pancreatic gene regulation.
literature.bearsOn: Background on PDX1 as a regulator; no NPY result.

literature.finding: A Y1 receptor agonist was studied in islets of diet-induced obese mice.
literature.bearsOn: NPY signaling acts on islets under high-fat diet, matching the re-expression result.

literature.finding: FoxO1 overexpression in hypothalamus and pancreas causes obesity and glucose intolerance.
literature.bearsOn: A shared upstream regulator that spans both the neuropeptide and the islet axis is a candidate mechanism.

literature.finding: NPY and its Y1 and Y2 receptors are expressed in pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive pancreatic cancer in a mouse model and human samples.
literature.bearsOn: Second tissue context in which NPY and pancreatic lineage genes co-occur.

literature.finding: A high-content beta-cell replication platform that uses PDX1 as a beta-cell marker.
literature.bearsOn: A ready assay format for the replication readout.

literature.finding: Extracellular Pdx1 and Npy mRNA in medium conditioned by insulin-producing cells tracks cell number and function.
literature.bearsOn: Both genes are measurable in the same cultures with established RT-PCR.

literature.finding: Methods chapter for RT-PCR of extracellular mRNAs including Pdx1 and Npy from insulin-producing cells.

NPY|PDX1.hypothesis: NPY expression in beta cells is inversely tied to PDX1 level: low PDX1 and immature beta cells express NPY, and mature PDX1-high cells do not.
assays: Triple immunostain NPY, PDX1 and MAFB in mouse islets at P0, P30 and after high-fat diet, scoring the fraction of NPY-positive cells inside PDX1-low and PDX1-high bins.
Pdx1 knockdown in a beta-cell line, with NPY mRNA by qPCR; the reverse knockdown of NPY with PDX1 and insulin readouts.
PYY-versus-NPY separation with isoform-specific probes, because the 2013 antibody cannot tell them apart.
controls: Non-rhyme beta-cell gene pair as a negative wire control
INS and POMC as the known positive wire
NPY on chr7 and PDX1 on chr13, so a locus effect is not expected
NPY|PDX1.falsifier: No change in NPY after Pdx1 manipulation, or NPY-positive cells equally common in PDX1-high and PDX1-low bins.

APP|TMPRSS2.reason: No shared disease rail and both genes sit on chr21. A positive result would not separate wiring from locus.
APP|TMPRSS2.ifRun: Add a chr21 non-rhyme pair as a locus control before reading any signal.

newRhymes.label: PDX1↔POMC
newRhymes.role: Endocrine neighbor of the thickened pair; POMC is the control gene in INS↔POMC.

newRhymes.label: POMC↔NPY
newRhymes.role: Closes a triangle with NPY↔PDX1 and PDX1↔POMC. NPY and POMC neurons are a textbook antagonistic pair in appetite control, so this rhyme is expected to be known; STRING was not queried here.

newRhymes.label: DNMT1↔PDX1
newRhymes.role: Low-coupling Pilot neighbor of PDX1 (epigenetic regulator). A follow-up candidate, not a support.
